title: Stable angina — exertional substernal chest pain (USMLE CVS case)

properties.cases overview: 58M with occasional substernal chest pain during strenuous activity; obesity, HTN, DM; fast-food diet and little exercise → classic stable angina due to fixed atherosclerotic coronary stenosis with exertional demand ischemia.
properties.feedback:
Key feedback points from our discussion:
- Corrected concept: stable angina is due to fixed stenosis with exertional demand mismatch, not plaque rupture/acute thrombosis (that is unstable angina/NSTEMI).
- Corrected ECG concept: stable angina typically shows ST depression (subendocardial ischemia) during pain/exertion and can be normal at rest.
- Added missing differential: vasospastic (Prinzmetal) angina = episodic coronary vasospasm causing rest pain and transient ST elevation; responds to CCB/nitrates.
